blocks.prompt: 3. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y}\).
blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle right side ko dekhiye: \(e^{x - y}\).
Exponents ke qanoon se \(e^{x - y} = e^x e^{-y}\), yani yeh sirf-\(x\) aur sirf-\(y\) functions ka zarb hai.
Is liye equation separable hai (yahi equation Question 1(iv) mein thi).
Plan: \(e^y\,dy = e^x\,dx\) bana kar dono taraf integrate karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y}\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: Exponential ko exponents ke qanoon se torenge; is se equation separable ban jayegi, phir alag kar ke integrate karenge.

Exponential ko torein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{e^x}{e^y}\]
Kyun: \(e^{x - y} = e^x \cdot e^{-y}\), aur negative power ka matlab neeche jana hai: \(e^{-y} = \frac{1}{e^y}\).

Variables alag karein
\[e^y\,dy = e^x\,dx\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(e^y\,dx\) se multiply kiya. \(e^y\) left par \(dy\) ke saath aa gaya aur \(dx\) right par \(e^x\) ke saath.
Dhyan dein: \(e^y\) ko upar le jana hai, \(e^{-y}\) ko \(dy\) ke saath chhorna nahi; dono taraf zarb sahi tarah karein.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int e^y\,dy = \int e^x\,dx\]
\[e^y = e^x + C\]
Kyun: \(e^u\) ka integral wohi \(e^u\) hota hai, kyunke \(e^u\) ki derivative bhi \(e^u\) hai. Ek hi constant \(C\) right side par lagaya.

Tasdeeq
\(e^y = e^x + C\) ko differentiate karein:
\[e^y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y}\]
Kyun: Chain rule se \(e^y\) ki derivative \(e^y\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai. \(e^y\) se divide karne par di hui equation wapas mil gayi.
